sentences.text: Heard Mr.V.R.Rajasekaran, leaned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsels appearing for the respondents.
3. The petitioner is manufacturing Sago.

On 21.08.2018, there was an inspection conducted by the 2nd and 3rd respondents at the Unit of the petitioner and the samples of Tapioca Starch milk  an intermediate product were taken also by seizing the Wet starch stock of 12.6 tons by entrusting the same to the petitioner for safe custody.
The samples so taken were sent for analysis.
The 4th respondent gave analysis report dated 27.09.2018 and expressed that the sample is found to be substandard and unsafe.

The 2nd respondent furnished a copy of the Analysis Report to the petitioner, so as to enable them to file their objection under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 r/w Rule 2.4.6 of the Food Safety and Standards Rules.
The petitioner filed objection on 09.11.2018 before the 2nd respondent, against the analysis report.

They made a further representation on 10.11.2018 to the 1st respondent seeking orders under http://www.judis.nic.in Section 29(6) and Section 30 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, for immediate release of the stock of Wet Tapioca Starch of 12.6 tons seized on 21.08.2018.
As the representation of the petitioner dated 10.11.2018 was not considered, the petitioner has filed the present writ petition.

4. Mr.V.R.Rajasekaran, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that even though the petitioner has made an objection on 09.11.2018 before the 2nd respondent, it is better that the 1st respondent to consider the objection and pass orders, since the 2nd respondent has already given a police complaint against the petitioner's son.

5. On the other hand, the learned Additional Advocate General, Mr.A.Kumar appearing for the contesting respondents submitted that since, there was physical restraint by the petitioner's son and others against the officials in exercising their statutory duty in some other place, the said criminal complaint was filed.

Therefore,he submitted that filing of such criminal complaint cannot be a reason to seek for disposing the objection filed by the petitioner by the 1st respondent, instead of the Designated Officer, appointed for such purpose, viz., the 2nd respondent.

6. Heard both sides.
7.

The petitioner is aggrieved against the order of seizure passed by the 2nd respondent in taking the samples and also sending the same for analysis and consequently, the petitioner is also aggrieved against the said http://www.judis.nic.in report.

8. Perusal of the communication issued by the 2nd respondent dated 08.10.2018, which is also impugned in this writ petition, would clearly shows that such report was forwarded to the petitioner only for the purpose of filing the appeal against such report, if they are aggrieved against the same.
Therefore, it is apparent that the petitioner's right to agitate against the report by raising all the points is not taken away.
Hence, the petitioner can raise all the objections, as raised in this Writ Petition, before the 2 nd respondent.
It is further seen that such objection was already filed on 09.11.2018 and same is pending before the 2nd respondent.

Needless to say that, it is for the 2nd respondent to consider the same on merits and in accordance with law and pass orders without having any prejudice against the petitioner on the reason that a criminal complaint was filed by him Sri Venkatachalapathy Rice And Sogo ... vs The Commissioner Of Food Safety on 11 February, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70817300/
3 against the petitioner's son and others as stated supra.

sentences.text: Needless to say that while discharging his official function in disposing the objection/appeal filed against the analysis report, he should apply his mind to the facts and circumstances and the position of law and thereafter, pass orders accordingly.
http://www.judis.nic.in 9

. Thus, without expressing any view on the rival contentions raised by both the parties, this Writ Petition is disposed of by directing the 2nd respondent to treat the objections filed by the petitioner on 09.11.2018 as the appeal filed under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
If any fees is to be paid by the petitioner along with the said appeal, the same shall be paid within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
On receipt of such fees if any, the 2 nd respondent shall pass orders on the appeal within a period of four weeks, thereafter.
It is open to the petitioner to raise further objections if any, against the analysis report along with the fees.
After getting the order from the 2nd respondent, it is open to the petitioner to work out in accordance with law, if they are aggrieved against the said order.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
